brief: Separate a premium from a deductible or excess.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Insurance Payments"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Prima y deducible son distintos"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Prêmio e franquia são distintos"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Separate a premium from a deductible or excess.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Paying for coverage and paying your share of a covered loss are separate costs; use the contract to distinguish them.
instruction.misconception: The premium is refunded if no claim occurs, or paying it removes the deductible.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: A premium buys coverage under the contract. A deductible is a stated share you retain when the covered loss occurs.
The premium is the stated price of coverage.
The deductible remains separate from the premium under these terms.
These terms explicitly make the premium nonrefundable.
Both costs remain distinct obligations under the stated policy.
A lower premium can leave a larger claim cost to fund.
The coverage price differs from the share retained per claim.
